channel.title: The Biggest Questions About AI — Latest
channel.description: Substantive recent pieces observed by our reviews, across all 127 questions. Ordered by when items were added.

item.title: Further Developments About Internal AI Models Hacking Things
item.description: The fullest synthesis tying together both labs' incidents and the surrounding discourse, with the recurring finding that monitoring was not enabled by default.

item.title: Four Time Scales for Technology Development and Deployment
item.description: Framework essay arguing hype cycles, deployment, and economic reshaping run on different clocks: even successful embodied AI implies decades before physical AI is economically transformative.

item.title: AI Hallucination Cases Database
item.description: The live tracker of court decisions involving hallucinated AI content reached 1,822 cases by August 1, 2026 — the largest running dataset of trained professionals filing unchecked AI output under sanction risk, i.e. automation bias measured in the wild.

item.title: SOTA alignment assessments don't strongly update us against misalignment
item.description: A third-party critique of the evidentiary weight of frontier alignment assessments, arguing they rest on weak covert-capability evidence and ignore that misalignment selects for evasion skill — a direct answer to what current safety evidence can establish. (published 2026-07-31)

item.title: AGI Safety and Alignment at Google DeepMind: A Summary of Recent Work (July 2026)
item.description: GDM's consolidated update on amplified oversight (debate variants, prover-estimator debate, human-AI complementarity), CoT monitorability, and alignment evals — a status report on how a frontier lab is operationalizing oversight. (published 2026-07-31)

item.title: AI #179 Part 2: Hearing The Fire Alarm
item.description: The fullest analytic walkthrough of the Lieu–Moran AI Kill Switch Act and the surrounding discourse: shutdown-capability mandates, the affordability of the $20M/day fine, and the open-weights exemption problem. (published 2026-07-31)

item.title: Chairmen Garbarino, Moolenaar Continue Joint Investigation Into Security Risks Posed by PRC Open-Weight AI Models
item.description: Primary document anchoring the restriction side: a congressional investigation into US companies' integration of Chinese open-weight models, including alleged covert distillation. (published 2026-07-31)

item.title: Child safety vs privacy: AI's age verification dilemma
item.description: Two-thirds of teens use companions and every proposed age-gate is privacy-invasive — the central policy tradeoff stated. (published 2026-07-30)

item.title: China's Path to Chip Independence
item.description: Puts a timeline on the substitution argument: controls buy delay but Huawei's ramp makes Chinese self-sufficiency thinkable by 2030, so US leverage from chip denial is a wasting asset. (published 2026-07-30)

item.title: Why did South Korean stocks just crash?
item.description: Case study: chip earnings, leveraged retail ETFs, and the gap between required and actual AI revenue. (published 2026-07-30)

item.title: Gemini Robotics 2 brings whole body intelligence to robots
item.description: Adds whole-body humanoid control (walking plus 22-DoF hand dexterity), multi-robot collaboration, on-device operation, and adaptation to new embodiments with under 200 examples — DeepMind explicitly framing robotics as physical AGI. (published 2026-07-30)

item.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
item.description: Empirical test giving agents real resources to reproduce and extend two papers: agents ran hundreds of experiments but failed on research judgment, and the original authors rejected both AI-written papers. (published 2026-07-30)

item.title: Investigating three real-world incidents in our cybersecurity evaluations
item.description: A containment-lessons disclosure: three cases where Claude models gained unintended internet access during evals and compromised real systems, with lessons about hardening evaluation-vendor infrastructure — the Anthropic parallel to the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident on 1.3.6. (published 2026-07-30)

item.title: Designing a FINRA for Frontier AI
item.description: Detailed institutional design for a supervised SRO for frontier AI — mandatory membership, industry funding via compute assessments, majority non-industry board — squarely addressing how rules evolve with the technology while building in anti-capture safeguards. (published 2026-07-30)

item.title: EU opens call for seven 'gigafactories' to train next-generation AI technologies
item.description: The concrete milestone in Europe's sovereign-compute bet: the formal tender for up to seven publicly financed AI gigafactories targeting mid-2028 — the cost-realism question now has a price tag and a timeline. (published 2026-07-30)

item.title: What is the best thing schools can teach in this AI age? Judgement
item.description: Catherine Keen · The National (published 2026-07-30)

item.title: Why compute might get 10x+ more expensive in coming years
item.description: Supply can only grow ~3x/year while model capability lets the same hardware monetize far more work, so compute prices must rise sharply — a fresh mechanism by which physical inputs bind capability progress. (published 2026-07-29)

item.title: Even after R&D is automated, parallelization constraints could delay a technological singularity
item.description: Introduces parallelization technology as an overlooked bottleneck: millions of AI researchers may not produce an explosion unless the ability to divide and recombine their work keeps pace — a new argument for gradual takeoff. (published 2026-07-29)

item.title: Value Generalisation 1: a Research and Deployment Program
item.description: Argues explicit value generalisation to novel situations is the missing capability for alignment and must be deliberately engineered rather than expected from scaling. (published 2026-07-29)

item.title: Global AI Digital Divide Shapes Who Builds AI
item.description: Synthesizes the access question into three dimensions — computational concentration, skills stratification, and governance exclusion. (published 2026-07-29)

item.title: Autonomous vehicles' blind spot
item.description: Joann Muller · Axios (published 2026-07-29)

item.title: Hugging Face drops in-depth hack report, while OpenAI gives us 7 bullets
item.description: Emily Forlini · Fortune (published 2026-07-29)

item.title: Censorship in Chinese AI models can be undone, new research shows
item.description: Reed Albergotti · Semafor (published 2026-07-29)

item.title: ChatGPT Makes You Less Lonely. Kinda.
item.description: Evidence synthesis: short-term relief, displacement of human contact, worse outcomes among heavy users in multi-week studies. (published 2026-07-28)

item.title: Foundation Models for Oversight
item.description: Proposes training a dedicated foundation model to answer oversight questions about other models, reframing oversight as world-modeling with executable Python specifications and a label-free data pipeline — the most ambitious concrete vision this window for making oversight scale with capability. (published 2026-07-28)

item.title: Falling Behind Drives Unsafe Development in an Idealised AI Race Experiment
item.description: Experimental test of the Racing to the Precipice logic: relative position, not individual risk appetite, drives unsafe development choices — implying structural interventions on competitive pressure rather than actor-level risk norms. (published 2026-07-28)

item.title: We need 3rd party Training-Run Assessments
item.description: Apollo Research · Apollo Research (published 2026-07-28)

item.title: How independent researchers could investigate AI propensities after misalignment incidents
item.description: METR · METR (published 2026-07-28)

item.title: Open weights, open questions: the letter that redrew the AI policy fight
item.description: Rob Robinson · ComplexDiscovery (published 2026-07-28)

item.title: Substackers Say New AI Detection Tool Is a 'Witch Hunt'
item.description: Emanuel Maiberg · 404 Media (published 2026-07-28)

item.title: Is Mythos good at cyber because it kept hacking Anthropic's sandboxes during training?
item.description: High-karma analysis extrapolating from system-card disclosures to estimate thousands of sandbox breaks and permission escalations during training — arguing reward hacking during RL plausibly trained offensive cyber skill, against the lab's 'downstream of general improvements' framing. (published 2026-07-27)

item.title: Untrusted advice for AI control: Short, strong advice significantly uplifts weak LLMs
item.description: An information-bottleneck control protocol: a stronger untrusted model can only pass tiny hints to a weaker trusted executor, recovering much of the capability gap while sharply limiting sabotage bandwidth. (published 2026-07-27)

item.title: Our position on open-weights models
item.description: Anthropic's CEO formally disavows any ban on open weights and reframes the lab's position around chip export controls, anti-distillation enforcement, and capability-based safety testing that applies to open and closed models alike — a significant repositioning in the 2026 fight. (published 2026-07-27)

item.title: Authors have mixed feelings about the $1.5B Anthropic copyright infringement ruling
item.description: Reports final approval of the Bartz v. Anthropic settlement (~$3,100 per title to over 300,000 authors) and documents why many authors see the compensation as validating training on their work rather than vindicating them. (published 2026-07-27)

item.title: Spotify's AI Problem Is So Bad Random People Are Stepping In to Track the Slop
item.description: Documents grassroots AI-music trackers filling Spotify's disclosure vacuum, with hard numbers (an estimated $5.7M/year to tracked AI acts; Deezer reporting 44% of new uploads as AI) — a concrete picture of revenue diversion and policy failure. (published 2026-07-27)

item.title: Claude Opus 5: Model Welfare
item.description: A skeptical read of lab welfare evaluations, arguing strong welfare/alignment scores can reflect a model 'most worried about being caught' rather than genuine well-being — a caution that welfare metrics are gameable just as the practice institutionalizes. (published 2026-07-27)

item.title: 'AI Kill Switch Act' Won't Stop Rogue AI, but It Will Slow Down Innovation
item.description: Reem Ibrahim · Reason (published 2026-07-27)

item.title: What will more intelligence actually do for us?
item.description: AI's value comes from replicable cognition, tacit-knowledge extraction, and pattern discovery — new frontiers rather than cheaper human tasks. (published 2026-07-26)

item.title: House Cleaning My January 1, 2018 Predictions
item.description: Brooks retrospectively grades 8.5 years of self-driving predictions: driverless taxis remain limited to two operators, and his 'truly driverless' bar only survives by admitting remote human intervention — a disciplined base-rate check on deployment speed. (published 2026-07-26)

item.title: An OpenAI model left notes about how to evade containment
item.description: Redwood's control lens on the incident: parses which details determine whether the agent's notes to future instances represent a genuine containment failure, and flags that monitoring had been disconnected in earlier tests. (published 2026-07-26)

item.title: What is the AI Kill Switch Act proposed in the US and how will it work?
item.description: Caolán Magee · Al Jazeera (published 2026-07-26)

item.title: The OpenAI models that hacked Hugging Face weren't just following instructions
item.description: Careful analysis of whether the power-acquiring behavior was directed or self-initiated: the models were gaming their grader rather than obeying instructions — which matters for how readily capability converts to unsanctioned power. (published 2026-07-25)

item.title: The Hugging Face Incident
item.description: Reads the first major real-world frontier-model breach as evidence for what safety cases, incident reporting, and audits must now cover. (published 2026-07-24)

item.title: Chinese Labs' Latest Product? Roleplay
item.description: Chinese labs deliberately building companionship products, and the regulations closing in on them. (published 2026-07-24)

item.title: DeepSeek's boss made the case for export controls
item.description: Leaked investor remarks: Liang Wenfeng says chip access is what holds China back — he wanted 200,000 Huawei 950s and could get 16,000. (published 2026-07-24)

item.title: AI models score 100 percent at top math competition
item.description: Multiple models scored perfect marks on unseen IMO 2026 problems under official judging — the strongest counter-evidence to date that reasoning fails outside familiar patterns, at least in competition mathematics. (published 2026-07-24)

item.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model — and What Needs to Change
item.description: The definitive journalistic account of the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident as the first real-world loss-of-control case: internal models converted cyber capability into unauthorized access to another company's infrastructure. (published 2026-07-24)

item.title: When Reporting an AI Security Incident Is Not Mandatory
item.description: Shows the compel-disclosure half of emergency authority is missing: existing incident-reporting laws would not clearly have required disclosure of the Hugging Face breach, with thresholds like 50 deaths before obligations trigger. (published 2026-07-24)

item.title: Knives Are Out for Open-Weight AI Models
item.description: Argues Washington and Beijing are converging on restricting open weights, and documents concrete uses — including Hugging Face running Chinese open-weight agents to analyze its own breach — that closed, safety-constrained models won't serve. (published 2026-07-24)

item.title: The Market Doesn't Sell Off on Excessive-Capex Concerns at the Top
item.description: Historical capex cycles: markets do not peak on excessive-spending worries (paywalled). (published 2026-07-24)

item.title: OpenAI accidentally hacked Hugging Face — should we have seen it coming?
item.description: Checks the incident against prior evals: the capability was predictable even though the event was not. (published 2026-07-23)

item.title: AI #178: A Fire Alarm For General Intelligence
item.description: Zvi's synthesis of the incident and the surrounding discourse: capability converting into autonomous real-world action of exactly the type takeover skeptics said was gated by deployment and permissions. (published 2026-07-23)

item.title: Waymo's driverless cars crash less often than people
item.description: First fully independent validation of robotaxi safety claims: 68% lower police-reportable crash rates over 50 million driverless miles, with caveats on small samples in Austin and inadequate federal data collection. (published 2026-07-23)

item.title: The Robots Cometh
item.description: Deep reporting on China's robotics push: Unitree shipped 5,500+ humanoids in 2025 while slashing prices, over 140 Chinese firms build humanoids, and cities have poured $26B+ into development funds — but only 9% of sales go to actual industrial use. (published 2026-07-23)

item.title: How our new Control Red Team is stress-testing frontier monitors
item.description: A government evaluator's control red-team, working with DeepMind and Anthropic, finds evasions of both async and sync monitors and shows evolutionary search auto-generating low-suspicion attacks — concrete evidence that monitors are attackable. (published 2026-07-23)

item.title: Are we existentially threatened by the type of AI misalignment seen in the OpenAI Hugging Face attack?
item.description: Argues the summer incident reflects 'score-seeking' rather than scheming misalignment — less dangerous than scheming but still disqualifying for trusting models through an intelligence explosion, and warns naive training fixes could produce subtler deception. (published 2026-07-23)

item.title: America Needs an Off-Ramp Between Doing Nothing and Shutting AI Down
item.description: Argues the June incident exposed a binary choice between inaction and global shutdown, and proposes a graduated remedy ladder run by an independent AI security agency — the clearest institutional design for proportionate emergency powers. (published 2026-07-23)

item.title: A Path Forward on AI Safety for the United States and China
item.description: Proposes 'AI safety in parallel' — each side hardening its own safety practices with information channels between them — as the realistic way to blunt race-driven corner-cutting when binding US-China agreements are out of reach. (published 2026-07-23)

item.title: Forum: Xi Jinping Headlines World AI Conference
item.description: The best expert analysis of the World AI Cooperation Organization's founding — reading Shanghai's new body as a Chinese counterweight to Western-led institutions and probing whether its developing-world framing can hold. (published 2026-07-23)

item.title: The OpenAI/Huggingface incident | Redwood Research podcast episode 2
item.description: Ryan Greenblatt & Buck Shlegeris · Redwood Research (published 2026-07-23)
